eras.title: Gospel
eras.summary: After a born-again Christian conversion in the late 1970s, Dylan made three albums of faith-centred songs and for a time played only that new material in concert. The period won him a Grammy and also alienated many fans who wanted the old songs.

moments.title: Saturday Night Live: three gospel songs
moments.text: On October 20, 1979, he played three songs from Slow Train Coming as the musical guest on Saturday Night Live.

moments.title: Gospel-only shows at the Warfield
moments.text: Starting November 1, 1979, he played a run of concerts at San Francisco's Fox Warfield Theatre made up only of new religious songs and none of his older hits.

moments.title: Grammy for Gotta Serve Somebody
moments.text: In February 1980 he won the Grammy for Best Rock Vocal Performance, Male, for Gotta Serve Somebody and performed the song at the ceremony.

moments.title: Older songs return to the set
moments.text: In November 1980 he returned to the Warfield for shows that brought some of his older songs back alongside the gospel material.

albums.title: Slow Train Coming
albums.why: His first album after becoming a born-again Christian, it set evangelical lyrics to a polished R&B sound cut at Muscle Shoals with producers Jerry Wexler and Barry Beckett. Mark Knopfler's guitar and a Grammy-winning single made it a commercial success even as it divided longtime fans.

albums.title: Saved
albums.why: A fuller gospel record, cut with his touring band and backing singers, that captures the fervor of the gospel-only concerts.

albums.title: Shot of Love
albums.why: Mixing faith songs with secular ones, it closed the gospel period and ends with Every Grain of Sand.

songs.title: Gotta Serve Somebody
songs.note: It won Dylan the 1980 Grammy for Best Rock Vocal Performance, Male.
songs.preview: Whoever you are and however high you rise, you will end up answering to one master or another.

songs.title: Precious Angel
songs.note: Mark Knopfler of Dire Straits plays the lead guitar on the track.
songs.preview: A thank-you to the woman who showed him the way to faith, mixed with warnings for a world he thinks has lost its bearings.

songs.title: I Believe in You
songs.note: It was one of three songs he played on Saturday Night Live in October 1979.
songs.preview: He holds to his belief even as friends turn away and treat him as a stranger.

songs.title: Slow Train
songs.note: The album takes its name from this song.
songs.preview: A survey of greed, false leaders and moral drift, with a reckoning steadily drawing closer.

songs.title: Gonna Change My Way of Thinking
songs.note: He recorded a reworked version as a duet with Mavis Staples for a 2003 tribute album of his gospel songs.
songs.preview: A vow to turn his life around and live by a new set of rules.

songs.title: When You Gonna Wake Up
songs.note: He performed it on Saturday Night Live in October 1979.
songs.preview: A list of society's hypocrisies, ending in a demand that the listener open their eyes.

songs.title: Man Gave Names to All the Animals
songs.note: It was published as an illustrated children's picture book in 2010.
songs.preview: A playful retelling of the first man naming each creature he meets in the garden.

songs.title: When He Returns
songs.note: The album's closing track is just Dylan's voice and Barry Beckett's piano.
songs.preview: A quiet hymn of surrender, waiting for a promised return that will set things right.

songs.title: Saved
songs.note: The title track is co-credited to Dylan and bassist Tim Drummond.
songs.preview: A jubilant testimony of being pulled out of a lost life.

songs.title: Solid Rock
songs.note: It was a driving fixture of the 1979–80 gospel concerts.
songs.preview: He declares he is holding on to an unshakable foundation no matter what the world throws at him.

songs.title: Pressing On
songs.note: In the 2007 film I'm Not There it is sung by John Doe.
songs.preview: A determined promise to keep moving toward a higher goal despite doubters.

songs.title: Shot of Love
songs.note: The title track was produced by Bumps Blackwell, known for his work with Little Richard.
songs.preview: A plea for the one kind of cure that can heal a troubled soul.

songs.title: Lenny Bruce
songs.note: It is a tribute to the comedian Lenny Bruce, who died in 1966.
songs.preview: A fond remembrance of a rule-breaking comic who was hounded in life and is missed now that he is gone.

songs.title: Every Grain of Sand
songs.note: It closes the album and is often counted among his finest songs.
songs.preview: A humble meditation on finding a guiding design in every small detail of an imperfect life.

songs.title: Serve Yourself
songs.note: John Lennon recorded it as a home demo in 1980 and it was released after his death.

songs.title: Every Grain of Sand
songs.note: Emmylou Harris recorded it for her 1995 album Wrecking Ball.

links.why: John Lennon wrote Serve Yourself as a sardonic rejoinder to Gotta Serve Somebody.
Emmylou Harris recorded the song on her acclaimed 1995 album Wrecking Ball.
Both songs from Slow Train Coming warn listeners that no one can avoid a moral choice.
